newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies called lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies called lower.

text.p: CME lean hog and pork belly futures were called lower in reaction to a week-long decline in cash pork prices and forecasts for $0.50 to 1.00 per cwt cash hog prices at Midwest markets Friday, analysts said.

Some analysts cautioned that follow-through buying from Thursday's late gains could occur early. Also, talk that supplies of market-ready hogs may decrease next week could provide some buying incentive in the futures.
Midwest cash dealers were calling cash hog prices lower Friday because of expected light Saturday slaughter amid the lower pork prices.
USDA reported pork cutout values late Thursday were down $0.71 to $0.70 per cwt. The cutout value for Grade 1 carcasses closed Thursday at $76.65 versus $79.27 a week ago.
Pork belly futures were called lower because of lower cash belly prices.
However, several analysts said the drop in cash prices has spurred demand by bacon processors. This may prevent a repeat of Thursday's steep declines in futures, they said.
In the USDA pork cutout report late Thursday, 12- to 14-lb fresh bellies were quoted at $84.00 per cwt down $2.50 from Wednesday.
